samples.brief: Two friends at a railway station discover their tickets are for different destinations.

sourceChapter.title: Dos billetes diferentes
sourceChapter.story:
Ana y Luis están en la estación. Ana tiene una bolsa. Luis tiene una mochila. Los dos amigos quieren viajar a Madrid.

—Yo tengo mi billete —dice Ana.

—Yo también tengo mi billete —dice Luis.

Ana mira su billete.

—Mi tren sale a las diez. ¿Y tu tren?

Luis revisa su billete. Luis mira la hora.

—Mi tren también sale a las diez.

Ana mira el billete de Luis. Ana ve un nombre: Toledo.

—Luis, ¿tu destino es Toledo?

—No, mi destino es Madrid.

—Pero tu billete dice «Toledo».

Luis mira su billete otra vez.

—Sí, es verdad. Mi billete es para Toledo. ¿Tu billete es para Madrid?

Ana muestra su billete.

—Sí. Mira: Madrid.

Los dos amigos miran los billetes.

—Tenemos dos billetes para dos destinos diferentes —dice Luis.

—Sí —dice Ana—. No podemos viajar juntos con estos billetes.

Luis ve una ventanilla. Una mujer está detrás de la ventanilla.

—Podemos preguntar allí —dice Luis.

Ana toma su bolsa. Los dos amigos caminan hacia la ventanilla.

content.title: Dos destinos diferentes
content.story:
Ana y Luis están en la estación. Ana lleva una bolsa. Luis lleva una mochila. Los dos amigos quieren viajar juntos a Madrid.

—¿Tienes tu billete? —pregunta Ana.

—Sí. Mi billete está aquí —dice Luis.

Luis saca su billete de la mochila. Ana mira su billete.

—Mi tren sale a las diez —dice Ana.

Luis mira la hora en su billete.

—Mi tren también sale a las diez.

—¿Y tu destino? —pregunta Ana.

—Madrid —responde Luis.

Luis muestra su billete. Ana mira el nombre del destino.

—Aquí dice «Toledo», Luis. No dice «Madrid».

Luis mira el billete otra vez.

—¡Es verdad! Mi billete es para Toledo.

Ana pone su billete al lado del billete de Luis.

—Mira. Mi billete es para Madrid. Tu billete es para Toledo.

—La hora es la misma, pero los destinos son diferentes —dice Luis.

—No podemos viajar juntos con estos billetes —dice Ana.

Luis mira una ventanilla. Una mujer está detrás de la ventanilla.

—¿Podemos cambiar mi billete? —pregunta Luis.

—No sé. Podemos preguntar allí —responde Ana.

Ana toma su bolsa. Luis guarda su billete. Los dos amigos caminan hacia la ventanilla.

glossary.meaning: And; connects people or ideas. In the question, it means 'and what about...?'
To be in a place. Están is used for the two friends; está for one person or ticket.
In or at; gives the location, including where information appears on a ticket.
The; agrees with the noun: el for masculine singular, la for feminine singular, and los for masculine plural.
Station; here, a railway station.
To carry or have a bag with you. Lleva is the present form for one person.
A or an; una is used before a feminine singular noun.
Bag.
Backpack.
Two.
Friend. Amigos is plural, referring to the two friends.
To want. Quieren means 'they want'; followed by viajar, it means they want to travel.
To travel; the infinitive follows quieren or podemos.
Together. Juntos has a masculine plural ending because it refers to both friends.
To; introduces the destination of travel.
To have. Tienes means 'you have,' addressing one person informally.
Your, addressing one person informally. Tu is capitalized at the start of a sentence and has no accent here.
Ticket; here, a train ticket. Billetes is plural.
To ask. Pregunta means 'asks'; preguntar is the infinitive after podemos.
Yes; an affirmative answer.
My; identifies the speaker's ticket or train.
Here; refers to the ticket's location or information written on it.
To say; for a ticket, to read or state something. Dice is the present form for one person or thing.
To take something out. Saca means 'takes out,' here from a backpack.
His or her; identifies the ticket or bag belonging to the person being discussed.
From or of; marks where the ticket comes from or whose ticket it is.
To look at. Mira means 'looks at' in narration; Mira in the dialogue is an informal command, 'look.'
Train.
To leave or depart. Sale means 'departs,' here referring to a train.
At ten o'clock; a las introduces a clock time.
Time; here, the train's departure time.
Also or too; says the second train leaves at the same time.
Destination; the place a journey goes to. Destinos is plural.
To answer or reply. Responde is the present form for one person.
To show. Muestra means 'shows,' here showing a ticket.
Name; here, the destination name printed on the ticket.
Of the; combines de and el. Here it connects 'name' with 'destination.'
Not; placed before a verb to make a negative statement.
Again; one more time.
To be; identifies destinations and describes the times and destinations. Es is singular; son is plural.
To be true. Es verdad expresses that Luis recognizes the ticket really says Toledo.
For; identifies the destination a ticket is valid for.
To put or place. Pone means 'places,' here putting one ticket beside the other.
Next to or beside. Del combines de and el before the masculine noun billete.
Same. Misma agrees with the feminine noun hora; la misma means 'the same.'
But; contrasts the matching times with the different destinations.
Different. Diferentes is plural because it describes destinos.
To be able to or can. Podemos means 'we can'; followed by an infinitive. No podemos means 'we cannot.'
With; here, using these tickets to travel.
This; estos means 'these' before a masculine plural noun such as billetes.
Service or ticket window at the station.
Woman.
Behind; describes the woman's position relative to the service window.
To change or exchange; here, to exchange the ticket for a suitable one.
To know. No sé means 'I don't know'; sé is the present form for 'I.'
There; refers to the service window where they can ask for help.
To take or pick up. Toma means 'picks up,' here taking her bag.
To put away. Guarda means 'puts away,' here putting the ticket away.
To walk. Caminan means 'they walk,' referring to both friends.
Toward; indicates the direction they walk.
